scenes.description: Cold open. A smiling paper flight attendant presents a coffee pot; on the word 'trained,' the pot snaps into a fire extinguisher and a tiny coral flame folds itself out.
scenes.framing: Medium-close character portrait, attendant left of center, service object large on the right; layered paper cabin wall in the background.
scenes.movement: Two-frame stop-motion replacement cut, slight hand-made registration jitter, one anticipatory dip before the object morph, then a held reaction.
scenes.transition_out: transform: extinguisher label expands into the title's coral underline
scenes.overlay_notes: Word-level captions low-center; punch label SAFETY CREW appears upper-right after the morph.
scenes.shot_intent: Deliver the brief's core reversal before the viewer can scroll away.
scenes.information_role: The visible service role conceals emergency capability.

required_assets.description: Layered paper attendant, coffee pot, fire extinguisher, flame, and cabin wall.

scenes.description: A torn-paper aircraft window opens like a storybook flap. The title assembles from mismatched cut-paper letters around it while a tiny aircraft glides behind the window.
scenes.framing: Centered circular window with title wrapping above and below; generous cream negative space.
scenes.movement: Paper flap opens, title pieces drop with staggered overshoot, aircraft crosses once, then the full card holds.
scenes.overlay_notes: Designed title only; captions temporarily move to the lower safe area and do not duplicate the entire title card.
scenes.shot_intent: Name the series premise and give the hook a clean visual landing.
scenes.information_role: This is a myth-busting episode about a widely misunderstood profession.

required_assets.description: Aircraft-window flap, cut-letter title, tiny moving aircraft silhouette.

scenes.description: Full paper crew figure stands beside a snack cart. The cart rolls aside to reveal a large shield-shaped SAFETY badge behind the character, with the FAA fact on a small pinned label.
scenes.framing: Medium-wide full figure on the right third; cart begins foreground-left; oversized badge occupies midground after reveal.
scenes.movement: Cart rolls with uneven stop-motion steps, character pivots toward the badge, badge scales up on a soft paper spring.
scenes.transition_out: slide: badge becomes the cover of a training scrapbook
scenes.overlay_notes: Small evidence label: MAIN DUTY: SAFETY. Word-level captions above the bottom UI zone.
scenes.shot_intent: State the authoritative thesis while preserving the friendly character focus.
scenes.information_role: The FAA defines passenger safety as the main duty.

character_actions.notes: Movement is paper replacement animation, not skeletal realism.

required_assets.description: Full crew character, snack cart, safety shield, pinned FAA label.

scenes.description: Overhead training scrapbook. Five tactile tabs flip in sequence: evacuation slide, emergency exit, extinguisher, first-aid cross, and AED/medical kit.
scenes.framing: Top-down full-page composition; icons occupy different clipped panels on a teal scrapbook spread, with a binder edge along the left.
scenes.movement: Tabs flip and stamp into place one per narration item; a torn WEEK 1 → WEEKS label stretches across the binding; final one-second hold.
scenes.transition_in: slide: safety badge opens as book cover
scenes.transition_out: transform: round AED pad becomes a cabin porthole seen from above
scenes.overlay_notes: Designed labels are single nouns only; captions sit on a cream strip at the bottom.
scenes.shot_intent: Make the breadth and duration of training tangible without turning the list into floating icons.
scenes.information_role: Training spans weeks and covers evacuation, fire, first aid, and medical response.

required_assets.description: Scrapbook spread, five training panels, binder, stamps, and labels.

scenes.description: An empty cream field becomes an overhead aircraft cabin: seats slide in from both sides, paper passengers pop into every row, and coral exit arrows appear at the corners.
scenes.framing: Extreme-wide overhead diagram, cabin centered vertically with clear margins; seats form two blue-teal columns around a cream aisle.
scenes.movement: Progressive geometric build: fuselage outline draws, seats insert, passengers populate, exits pulse once; camera is N/A beyond a subtle virtual dolly-in.
scenes.transition_out: slide: aisle stretches downward into a countdown track
scenes.overlay_notes: Small label: MORE THAN 44 SEATS. Captions float above the cabin tail, never over the diagram.
scenes.shot_intent: Establish that the 90-second rule concerns a full-capacity certification scenario, not an abstract number.
scenes.information_role: The certification context begins with a full aircraft above the regulatory seat threshold.

required_assets.description: Procedural paper cabin diagram, seat rows, passenger dots, exit arrows.

scenes.description: Hero moment. A giant coral paper timer fills the frame at 90 while miniature passengers stream through two torn-paper exits. The timer flips over to reveal CERTIFICATION TEST, then a smaller NOT EVERY REAL ACCIDENT caveat settles beneath.
scenes.framing: Extreme close-up on the timer face, slightly high angle; tiny cabin and moving figures occupy a lower paper layer for scale.
scenes.movement: Numbers slap down with weighted overshoot, figures travel on curved paper paths, timer card physically flips for the caveat, then motion calms for a two-second accuracy hold.
scenes.transition_out: transform: timer rim becomes an aircraft doorway arch
scenes.overlay_notes: Designed labels: 90 SECONDS, CERTIFICATION TEST, SIMULATED CONDITIONS. Captions move to the upper safe area during the caveat.
scenes.shot_intent: Create the memorable visual peak while immediately protecting the fact from the common real-accident misinterpretation.
scenes.information_role: Ninety seconds is a simulated certification and demonstration standard.

required_assets.description: Giant timer, miniature passengers, exit paths, flip-card caveat system.

scenes.description: At the aircraft doorway, the attendant greets three different paper passengers. Gentle thought-bubble cut-outs appear in turn: assistance, wellness, and exit-row readiness, with check marks rather than surveillance graphics.
scenes.framing: Over-shoulder view from behind the attendant at frame-left toward passengers entering from frame-right; bubbles occupy the upper half without covering faces.
scenes.movement: Passengers advance one at a time on a short tracking move; attendant nods and gestures; each bubble unfolds from the welcome mat and returns before the next.
scenes.transition_in: transform from timer rim to doorway arch
scenes.transition_out: transform: welcome mat folds into a horizontal timeline
scenes.overlay_notes: Three small labels: HELP, WELLNESS, EXIT ROW. Word-level captions remain low-center.
scenes.shot_intent: Reframe a familiar greeting as calm operational awareness without implying intrusive profiling.
scenes.information_role: The greeting can surface assistance needs, intoxication or illness concerns, and exit-row suitability.

character_actions.notes: All acting remains gentle and nonjudgmental.

required_assets.description: Doorway set, attendant and passenger cut-outs, three fold-out safety bubbles.

scenes.description: A split paper timeline shows BOARDING WORK already moving on the left while the MAIN HOURLY CLOCK on the right remains asleep. A cabin door slides shut at center and the coral clock springs awake; a NEWER CONTRACTS tab adds boarding pay as a current caveat.
scenes.framing: Wide horizontal split adapted to the vertical canvas: upper lane for boarding tasks, lower lane for the pay clock, aircraft door acting as the center hinge.
scenes.movement: Small task cards travel before the clock starts; door closes with a soft thump; clock hands begin; caveat tab slides in and partially overlaps the old rule.
scenes.transition_in: transform from welcome mat to timeline
scenes.transition_out: paper flip: timeline becomes a service tray
scenes.overlay_notes: Designed labels: BOARDING WORK, DOOR CLOSES, MAIN HOURLY CLOCK, SOME NEW CONTRACTS ADD BOARDING PAY. Captions use the top safe area for this lower-heavy diagram.
scenes.shot_intent: Make the hidden timing mismatch instantly understandable while preserving the 2026 caveat.
scenes.information_role: Traditional block-time pay can start after boarding work; newer contracts increasingly modify that arrangement.

required_assets.description: Two-lane pay timeline, door hinge, clock face, task cards, caveat tab.

scenes.description: A top-down service tray enters with a drink. It flips like a paper card to reveal the SAFETY CREW badge and a compact collage of extinguisher, first-aid kit, and exit arrow. A tiny tray table lowers for the next-episode tease.
scenes.framing: Centered overhead hero tray against a quiet cream background; final tray-table tease peeks from the bottom edge.
scenes.movement: Single satisfying card flip, safety icons fan out once, final words settle, then a small tray table click closes the episode.
scenes.transition_out: cut to cream on the tray-table click
scenes.overlay_notes: Final designed line: UNDERNEATH THE SMILE: RESCUE CREW. Next-episode strip: WHY YOUR TRAY TABLE MATTERS. Captions remain distinct and finish before the tease strip.
scenes.shot_intent: Resolve the service-versus-safety contrast and provide a concrete series handoff.
scenes.information_role: The visible hospitality is real, but the underlying professional identity is safety crew.

required_assets.description: Service tray card, drink, safety badge, three safety icons, tray-table tease.

metadata.animatic_rules: Each scene has an entrance under 0.6 seconds, one main transformation or progressive build, at least a 0.6-second information hold, and a physical paper exit. Registration jitter stays below 2 pixels and changes only every two frames.
metadata.transition_rules: Use only cut, slide, transform, and paper flip/peel. Transform transitions carry one object between narrative ideas; cuts are reserved for the hook and final click.
metadata.hold_rules: Hold the title for 1.2 seconds, MAIN DUTY label for 1.0 second, 90-second caveat for 2.0 seconds, boarding-pay caveat for 1.5 seconds, and final next-episode strip for 1.0 second.

tool_path_map.all_scenes: Hand-authored project-local Remotion React/SVG/CSS; no stock scene registry and no AI-generated plates.
tool_path_map.captions: word timings from narration transcript -> bespoke per-word caption renderer

metadata.signature_device: The giant reversible 90-second paper timer appears only in sc06.

primary_subjects: crew figure plus hidden safety badge

metadata.caption_safe_zone: Keep baseline above y=1660 and below y=1450 only when top-positioned; maximum two lines and five words per cluster.
